source.title_on_document: Uneven Gains of Generative Artificial Intelligence on Creativity Enhancement: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis (title page, PDF p. 1); the abstract page (PDF p. 4) heads it 'Uneven Gains of Generative Artificial Intelligence on Individual Creative Performance: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis'

supplement.where: Separate Supplementary material.pdf (35 pages), https://osf.io/download/nh53g/ (OSF file 69ca39971060ef889673fc5e; uploaded 2026-03-30, verified at https://api.osf.io/v2/files/69ca39971060ef889673fc5e/), read in memory. supplement.holds: Search strings; data-extraction methods; moderator definitions and coding criteria; design-specific effect-size formulas (S1.3, PDF pp. 5-6, printed pp. 4-5); descriptive plots; additional results and precision in Tables S5-S19 (PDF pp. 21-27), including Cook's-distance confidence intervals in Table S15 (PDF p. 25, printed p. 24); and protocol deviations in S2.9 (PDF pp. 28-33, printed pp. 27-32). It contains no study-by-study listing of per-condition means, SDs, and sample sizes. The v2 main text refers to S1.4 for protocol deviations (main PDF p. 18, printed p. 15), but S1.4 is Moderator variables in this later supplement (PDF pp. 7-18, printed pp. 6-17).

paper_design_summary: A PROSPERO-preregistered systematic review and three-level random-effects meta-analysis of 67 articles (115 independent studies, 322 effect sizes) published 2020 to October 31, 2025 that compare creative task performance in a human-only condition with a human-generative-AI collaboration condition. Effects are Hedges' g (human-AI minus human-only), with publication-bias correction by cluster-robust PET-PEESE and moderator analyses by task modality, domain, age group, expertise, AI intervention mode, and model version.

studies.label: Meta-analysis of human-only versus human-generative-AI creative performance (115 independent studies, 322 effect sizes)

participants.who: Included primary studies: 67 articles comprising 115 independent studies and 322 effect sizes, published 2020 to October 31, 2025; 86% published in peer-reviewed journals; samples of children and adults (no adolescent studies), novices and experts. Two studies of atypical populations (10 effect sizes) were analyzed separately and excluded from the main analysis. The PDF reports no total participant count in its text.
participants.quote: 67 articles were included, comprising 115 independent studies and yielding a total of 322 effect sizes.
participants.locator: PDF p. 19 (printed p. 16), Method, Literature search; also PDF p. 7 (printed p. 4), Results

ai_tool.name_model: Generative AI across included studies: GPT family (e.g., GPT-3.5 / GPT-4; ChatGPT), Claude, Stable Diffusion, DALL-E 2, StyleGAN, BigGAN (Table 1, PDF p. 33)
ai_tool.how_used: Varies by included study; coded as real-time use during the task or training/pre-task use before the task, and with or without division of labour (Table 2, PDF pp. 34-35)

task.description: Mixed creative tasks across included studies: divergent thinking (e.g., Alternative Uses Task, brainstorming), creative problem solving (e.g., Remote Associates Test, insight problems), and creative products (e.g., story writing, visual art, design); text-based, image-based, and multimodal outputs (Table 2, PDF p. 34)

synthesis.inclusion: English-language articles that provided enough data to compute effect sizes and empirically tested creativity-related task performance in both a human-only and a human-AI collaborative condition, where the AI is a generative AI system (e.g., large language models, image generators) supporting human participants in creative tasks. Excluded: studies of AI-only or human-only performance without a direct comparison, studies with no identifiable creativity measure, theoretical papers, reviews, meta-analyses, qualitative reports, commentaries, and simulations without experimental designs. Random assignment was not an inclusion criterion: it is one of four quality indicators used in a sensitivity analysis, and both independent-sample and paired-sample designs are included (PDF p. 19, printed p. 16; PDF pp. 24-25).

pooled.comparison: Overall: human-generative-AI collaboration vs human-only creative performance, three-level random-effects model, 322 effect sizes
pooled.what_it_standardizes: Hedges' g compares human-generative-AI collaboration with human-only creative performance. The separately read supplement uploaded 2026-03-30 (S1.3, PDF pp. 5-6, printed pp. 4-5) documents different standardizers: posttest-only effects divide the experimental-control mean difference by the sample-size-weighted pooled SD; controlled pretest-posttest effects divide the between-group difference in mean improvement by the weighted pooled pretest SD; the displayed paired-design formula divides the condition mean difference by sqrt(SD_exp^2 + SD_ctrl^2 - 2*r*SD_exp*SD_ctrl), the SD of the difference scores. Cohen's d is then multiplied by the Hedges correction factor J. The pooled g values therefore combine different standardization bases. This detail comes from the later supplement, extending the v2 main text's description of conversion from means, SDs, and t-values (main PDF p. 21, printed p. 18). Indicators mix originality, fluency, flexibility, appropriateness, elaboration, global creativity, and other measures; rater types include layperson, expert, self-report, and machine (main PDF pp. 34-35, Table 2). Paired designs use an assumed pre-post correlation, varied in sensitivity analyses (main PDF pp. 24-25, printed pp. 21-22).

eligibility.reason: Systematic review and meta-analysis with no original experiment assigning people to AI assistance (main PDF pp. 18-25, Method and Data Analysis); criterion 1 is not met for a primary study in this paper. Criteria 2 and 3 cannot be assessed for an original experiment because the paper reports none: study/effect-size counts are not participant counts, and the participant counts remain null. No primary estimate is coded; the paper's pooled Hedges' g values are recorded only in the synthesis block. Included studies mix randomized and non-randomized designs, independent and paired samples, and self-report with other rater types (main PDF pp. 10, 24-25, 35; later supplement uploaded 2026-03-30, S2.9, PDF p. 29, printed p. 28). The pooled effects also combine different standardization bases (later supplement S1.3, PDF pp. 5-6, printed pp. 4-5), so they are not directly comparable to the Atlas's randomized-only, output-scored primary estimates.

one_line_finding: Across 115 independent studies (67 articles, 322 effect sizes, published 2020 to October 2025), people working with generative AI scored higher on creative tasks than people working alone, Hedges' g = 0.62, 95% CI [0.46, 0.78], shrinking to g = 0.25, 95% CI [0.12, 0.37] after cluster-robust PET-PEESE correction (PsyArXiv v2, abstract PDF p. 4; Results PDF pp. 7-8; Bias tests PDF p. 23).
